messages:
Maya: Quick sync — we're bringing up the L6 reranker candidate and need to decide dataset mix for baseline evals. Longtail-heavy vs core-heavy? thinking about gating rules for NDCG/MRR regressions.
Tom: i'd vote for a 70/30 core:longtail eval split as default. core keeps product impact visible, longtail catches edge regressions. :+1:
Rory: agree with mix but we should report metrics per-slice not just aggregate. NDCG is sensitive to tail docs, might mask core regressions.
Iris: FYI in the quant experiments I ran last week we saw MRR@10 drop ~1.2% on short queries after PTQ; long queries were mostly unchanged. so slice-by-length is important. :thinking_face:
Tom: ok add buckets: short(<32 tok), mid(32-128), long(>128). compute NDCG@5/10, MRR@10, recall@100.
Maya: also need to lock query/doc formatting: do we include titles+snippets concat or only snippets? formatting differences changed scores previously.
Iris: include two variants: "preserve-title" (title + sep + snippet) and "snippet-only". run both, and a small ablation where we truncate title to 30 chars.
Tom: can we standardize tokenizer seeds & padding? the earlier mismatch was tokenizer-vocab shift. run with same tokenizer version and fixed random seed for sampling.
Rory: gating suggestion: no >0.5% NDCG@10 drop on core bucket, and no >1% MRR@10 drop on core. if thresholds hit, fail bring-up. also check stat significance (bootstrap p < 0.05).
Maya: nice. Iris can you paste the eval command you used?
Iris: sure — example:
```
python eval_rerank.py \\n  --model candidate-l6 \\n  --queries datasets/core_queries.json \\n  --docs datasets/core_docs.json \\n  --format preserve-title \\n  --metrics ndcg@10,mrr@10,recall@100 \\n  --buckets short,mid,long \\n  --seed 42 \\n  --bootstrap 1000
```
Tom: can eval-bot post a quick sanity run on the smaller core holdout (10k queries) so we have baseline numbers?
eval-bot: quick-run: candidate-l6 on core-10k | NDCG@10=0.821 (+0.3 vs prod), MRR@10=0.612 (-0.4 vs prod) | buckets: short:Mrr -1.1, mid:+0.6, long:+0.2
Maya: thanks. that MRR dip on short is worrying. Iris, can you repro locally with PTQ toggled? maybe quant config caused KV-cache rounding issue.
Iris: will run PTQ vs FP16 vs quant-ptq with same eval above. i'll post diffs.
Rory: also add a candidate-curation check: ensure candidate score distribution isn't shifted (mean, std) and percentage of empty candidates per query. shifts often explain metric regressions.
Tom: i'll set up the 3 eval configs in the CI matrix: core-only, longtail-only, mix-70-30, each with two formatting variants.
Maya: plan sounds good. timeline?
Tom: schedule runs tonight, collect outputs tomorrow morning US time. will share a short summary thread with per-slice deltas and decisions.
Maya: if baseline passes gates we proceed to canary with 5% traffic. if not, block and iterate. thanks all. :rocket:
